children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday after the bell. Here’s what to look for.

Northwest Bancshares beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $180.8 million, up 20.2% year on year. It was a satisfactory quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Northwest Bancshares a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Northwest Bancshares’s revenue to grow 9.2% year on year, slowing from the 20.8% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Northwest Bancshares rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at Northwest Bancshares’s peers in the thrifts & mortgage finance segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Ladder Capital delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 107%, beating analysts’ expectations by 53.9%, and WaFd Bank reported revenues up 17.6%, topping estimates by 8.3%. Ladder Capital’s stock price was unchanged after the resultswhile WaFd Bank was down 1%.

Investors in the thrifts & mortgage finance segment have had steady hands going into earnings, with share prices flat over the last month. Northwest Bancshares is up 1.1% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $16.29 (compared to the current share price of $15.48).
